LatticeBand.title: Periodic-lattice absorbing-band certificates and a base-9 Lychrel number
LatticeBand.scope: A third certificate format, proved sound for every base: templates B ++ band(W, l) ++ reverse B whose period block W (any length, here 4) is absorbing, i.e. the carry leaving W is one constant for either incoming carry, so no centre block and no flip condition are needed. The band length l is the first l entries of the periodic word W W W ..., and one reverse-and-add step maps the template to a template with a new block W2 = gen Y d, a new B2, and band length l + gm with phase (rho + gm) mod |W| (never shrinking). A cycle of checked edges (lcycleOK, evaluated by the kernel) yields a Lychrel template value for every band length l >= 2|W| in the right residue class (lychrel_of_lcycle). Instance: two explicit 10-edge cycles in base 9 (period block length 4, |B| = 61, overflow word 1100011000) give exists_lychrel9 : exists n, Lychrel 9 n for each, with Lychrel the unchanged Agent120.Neutral.Lychrel, plus one rejected wrong-phase certificate per cycle. Base 9 is not among the bases (11, 17, 20, 26, powers of two) for which, as far as Wikipedia and OEIS A060382 record, Lychrel existence was previously known; no literature search beyond that was done. Nothing is claimed about base 10 or 196: the decimal period-8 lattice exteriors need a periodic centre, and none is known.
